subject: Quarterly invoicing with escrow settlement — conditional offer
messages:
From: Sofia Diaz <sofia.diaz@helionai.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com; finance@helionai.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — quarterly invoicing + conditional Net-90 for pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helion is excited to move the pilot to production. Before we finalize, our finance team asked whether Redwood can bill on a quarterly cadence with a Net-90 remit for the first two quarters while our accounting system consolidates vendor payments.

Concretely:
- Quarterly invoices for usage (pdf attached)
- Payment window: 90 days from invoice date for Q1 and Q2
- We can put the first quarter payment into an escrow arrangement (we have legal ready to speak to your contracts team)
- In exchange, we’re asking for a 12% committed-volume discount across the pilot term

We understand this is non-standard; hoping to see what flexibility Redwood has. I attached our usage forecast and a short note from our procurement team.

Would you be able to route this for approvals? If helpful, I can loop in our controller (finance@helionai.com).

Best,
Sofia Diaz\VP, Procurement\Helion AI

Attachments: helion_quarterly_request.pdf (pdf), usage_estimate_q4.xlsx (xlsx)

From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request — quarterly invoicing + conditional Net-90 for pilot

Team — forwarding Helion’s ask. Summary: quarterly billing + Net-90 for first two quarters, escrow offer for Q1, and a 12% discount requested.

Immediate questions:
- Can finance accept quarterly invoice cadence operationally (Marissa)? Any headwinds on cashflow/collections?
- From deal desk: would we consider 12% on committed volume if they put Q1 into escrow and sign a 12-month minimum?
- Compliance/contracts: is an escrow note/legal touchpoint acceptable to mitigate risk (Jonas)?

Proposed quick options to surface to the customer:
A) Conditional Net-60 (instead of Net-90) for Q1/Q2, escrow on Q1, 8% committed discount
B) True quarterly invoicing + Net-90 but require a payment guarantee (escrow + corporate guarantor) and reduce discount to 5%
C) Standard monthly billing with a 10% prepayment credit applied to quarterly reconciliation — avoid Net-90 entirely

I’d like a decision or exec sign-off by EOD tomorrow if possible — sales is pushing to close this week. Attaching Helion files for context.

Thanks,
Irene Choi\Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Sales\Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: helion_quarterly_request.pdf, usage_estimate_q4.xlsx

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request — quarterly invoicing + conditional Net-90 for pilot

Irene / team — quick take from deal desk / sales ops. We should avoid open Net-90 unless mitigated. My suggested compromise (fast path to close):
- Accept quarterly invoicing for the pilot
- Offer Net-60 for Q1/Q2 (not Net-90) with the following safeguards:
  * Q1 paid into an escrow account established by Helion; funds released to Redwood on invoice approval or after 30 days following invoice acceptance
  * 8% committed-volume discount across the pilot (applies to committed minimum only)
  * If Helion misses >1 invoice beyond Net-60, we revert to monthly billing and remove discount prospectively
- Add an early-pay credit: 2% of invoice if paid within 15 days (encourages faster payment)

Rationale: keeps deal momentum, materially reduces exposure, and provides strong behavioral incentive. From a revenue recognition standpoint, escrow + invoice acceptance preserves our ability to forecast.

If accepted, we’ll need VP-level approval for the discount and confirmation from finance that the escrow/legal language is sufficient. Jon as legal lead — can your team prepare a boilerplate escrow addendum?

-Karthik\Director, Deal Desk\Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: proposed_mop_terms.docx (draft language to use as starting point)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request — quarterly invoicing + conditional Net-90 for pilot

Irene / team — finance response and conditional approval. After modeling cashflow and risk, finance will approve the following as an exception for HEL-3921: 
- Quarterly invoicing OK for the pilot period (Q1–Q2) provided an escrow instrument is in place for Q1 covering at least the committed-minimum invoice amount.
- Payment terms: Net-60 for Q1 and Q2. We will not accept Net-90 without additional corporate guarantee.
- Discount: approve up to 8% committed-volume discount (matches Karthik’s recommendation). Any higher discount requires VP Revenue sign-off (Marcus / Jonas).
- Early-pay credit: approve a 2% credit if paid within 15 days — finance to track and apply credit on next invoice.

Operational asks:
- Legal (Jonas) to produce an escrow addendum and a short guarantor template by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik / Irene: confirm deal term (12 months minimum) and committed-minimum numbers so finance can size the escrow amount.

Once the above are in place, Sales can present the conditional offer to Helion and attach a DocuSign path for the pilot SOW + escrow addendum.

Marissa Cole\Head of Finance — Commercial\Redwood Inference
